intro: You are a lone worker whenever you work without a colleague on hand, so plan for safety, keep in touch, and trust your instincts.
points: If a situation ever feels unsafe, leave calmly, raise the alarm on your device or phone, then report it.
No law bans lone working, but the Health and Safety at Work Act requires your employer to assess and control the risks.
Follow your safe systems every time: check in and out, carry a charged phone, share your schedule, and use your alarm.
Keep asking "does this feel safe right now?" as you arrive and during the visit, and act on the answer.
If a risk assessment says a visit needs two workers, it must never be attempted alone.
Report every incident and near miss the same day, factually, so the risk assessment is updated and the next worker protected.
